lines.say: Pac-Man was partly inspired by a pizza, with one slice missing.
It was designed by Toru Iwatani at Namco, in Japan.
He wanted a game that wasn't about shooting, so he made it about eating.
In Japan, it was first called Puck Man, from paku paku, the sound of chomping.
In America, the name was changed, because people worried vandals would scratch the P into a different letter.
The four ghosts don't move the same way. One chases you, one tries to cut you off, and one just wanders.
Guinness calls it the most successful coin-operated arcade game ever, with over 290,000 machines.

lines.say: Level 256 can't be beaten. A bug fills half the screen with garbage.
So the highest possible score is 3,333,360. You have to eat every dot, fruit and ghost, without dying once.
